meta.title: File Manager
meta.description: Browse, organize and upload your files, and choose which ones Leo uses.

allFiles.heading: All files
allFiles.emptyDescription: Upload files or drop them here. Then choose which ones Leo can use.

folders.heading: Folders
folders.emptyDescription: Create a folder to organize your files, or to let Leo read a whole set at once.
folders.dropHereLeo: Drop to move here. Leo will use it.
folders.leoReadsAll: Leo uses everything it can read in this folder

folder.notFoundDescription: It may have been deleted or renamed in another session.
folder.emptyLeo: Upload or move files here and Leo will use them.
folder.empty: Upload files here, drag them onto this folder in My files, or use Move to in a file’s menu.

leo.viaFile: Leo uses this file because you chose it
leo.viaFolder: Leo uses this file through its folder
leo.unknownType: Leo can’t read this type of file

menu.heldOverLimit: Leo stopped reading it: over your plan’s limit

dialogs.shareDescription: Leo answers from it in the workspace for whoever you choose. It stays here, stays yours, and leaves the workspace if you delete it or leave.
dialogs.transferDescription: It moves out of your files and belongs to {workspace}: it stays there when you leave, and its admins manage it. Other workspaces you shared it in lose it. You can’t undo this.

upload.uploading: Uploading {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}… {progress, number, percent}
upload.skippedDescription: Files that are empty or over {size} are skipped, and at most {max, number} upload at once.

picker.noFiles: No files yet. Upload some in File Manager first.

storage.label: Storage
storage.title: Storage
storage.overTitle: Your files are over your plan’s storage
storage.overDescription: Everything stays available and new uploads are paused. Free up space or choose a larger plan before {date}: after it, the newest files over the limit will be deleted.

leoLimit.title: Leo uses {used} of your files, more than the {limit} your plan includes
leoLimit.description: Leo keeps reading everything until {date}. Switch off files Leo doesn’t need or choose a larger plan: after that date, Leo stops reading the newest files over the limit. No file is deleted.
